chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A man entered the bathhouse, and hot water was poured over him, so the hair of his head and his beard fell out and never grew again. He said: "The diyah is upon him."

key_terms.فَلَا يَنْبُتُ أَبَدًا: it never grows again, indicating permanent damage
key_terms.مَاءٌ حَارٌّ: hot water that caused the injury
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation legally due for bodily injury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if hot water causes a man's head and beard hair to fall out permanently?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury that causes permanent loss of hair from the head and beard. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that compensation in the form of diyah is due for such irreversible harm.
